sector.name: PEB

fyPerformance: Q2 revenue was ₹505 Cr versus ₹491 Cr a year earlier; EBITDA was ₹41.7 Cr versus a similar prior-year quarter, with margin at 8.3% versus 8.5%.
H1 revenue was ₹965 Cr, up 10.7% YoY; H1 EBITDA was ₹81.1 Cr, up 10.7%, at an 8.4% margin. H1 PAT was ₹58.9 Cr versus ₹60.7 Cr.
Q2 volume was 41,600 tonnes, up about 1% YoY. The residual order book exceeded ₹2,000 Cr at 31 October, after the quarter ended.
highlights: Andhra Pradesh Phase 1 and both Gujarat phases were operational by the call; the Andhra heavy-structure plant began operations on 24 September.
Management identified roughly 15–20% of the residual order book as heavy-structure work, including data centers, a hospital, hotel and commercial buildings.
Management said the heavy-structure and export verticals should improve margin protection and operating leverage over time, while their start-up expenses are weighing on current-year margins.
Management retained its FY27 revenue execution goal of ₹2,150 Cr; it expects H2 execution to improve with seasonal clearances and a larger order book.
Interarch Building Solutions Ltd.whatChanged: The AP heavy-structure plant began commercial production on 24 September and both Gujarat phases were operational by the call, while management retained ₹2,150 Cr FY27 revenue execution despite flat Q2 EBITDA and costs incurred ahead of new-vertical revenue.
risks: Steel prices were unusually high and supply disruption raised inventory needs; only roughly 30–40% of the order book was described as variable-price, leaving a fixed-price portion exposed until repricing or execution.
Larger project billing cycles, higher steel inventories and new-plant ramp-up tied up working capital; net working capital after customer advances was about 44 days.
New-vertical design, selling and engineering expenses precede revenue, limiting near-term margin improvement despite the planned H2 execution ramp.

guidance.value: Improvement expected, but not beyond roughly 9–9.5%

fyPerformance: Q2 consolidated revenue reached ₹501.1 Cr, a quarterly record, up 15.5% YoY; H1 revenue was ₹867 Cr, up 18.9% YoY.

Q2 EBITDA excluding other income was ₹50.6 Cr, up 1.2%, at a 10.1% margin versus 11.5% a year earlier; Q2 margin improved from 9.4% in Q1. Q2 PAT was ₹29.6 Cr, up 0.4%; H1 EBITDA was ₹85.1 Cr (+5.1%) and PAT ₹47.8 Cr (+5.0%).
H1 gross margin fell around 2.3 percentage points as input costs increased faster than pass-through on existing orders.
H1 order inflow rose 71% to about ₹1,124 Cr; the September-end order book was ₹1,462.5 Cr, providing eight-to-nine months of stated visibility.

Operating cash flow was negative in H1 and working capital rose to about 60 days, above management's 40–55 day range; receivables backed by letters of credit and deliberate steel inventory accounted for much of the increase.
highlights: Ghiloth added 13,000 tonnes of steel processing capacity after Q2; management described sandwich-panel commissioning in late October, with commercial production from November and a ramp over the remaining fiscal months.
The Gujarat greenfield plant is planned to commission in Q4 FY27; first-phase capacity is 50,000 tonnes, within an 80,000-plus-tonne design.
Management expects H2 revenue and margins to improve as new orders reflect current input prices and steel inventory protects supply and costs.

Management expected a first structural-steel data-center supply order in Q3 and said existing facilities can serve the enquiries in hand without additional capex; the separate data-center subsidiary opportunity remained under discussion.
EPACK Prefab Technologies Ltd.whatChanged: Q2 margin recovered to 10.1% but missed the Q1 call’s 10.5–11.5% expectation, while management now guides FY27 margin at 10–10.5% and retains ₹1,900 Cr-plus revenue amid higher working capital and negative H1 operating cash flow.
risks: Steel and other input costs rose faster than pass-through on work already in execution, reducing gross margin by about 2.3 percentage points; price-escalation clauses are not yet standard.
Working capital reached about 60 days versus the 40–55 day range, and operating cash flow was negative in H1; management expects LC-related receivables to normalize in Q3.
Ghiloth and Gujarat capacity still need ramp-up; management said the Ghiloth panel-line ramp prioritizes volume and is not expected to lift margins during the ramp period.

guidance.value: 25–30% CAGR endeavor for the next couple of years

M&B Engineering Ltd.whatChanged: With FY27 revenue-growth guidance above 25% maintained, Sanand’s 20,000-tonne PEB expansion entered production on 26 October and new data-center/high-rise orders were secured after Q2, while freight and steel costs continued to temper margin recovery.
risks: Freight remained above pre-war levels despite easing from about USD12,000 to USD7,000–8,000 per container; management expects improvement but customers only absorb part of the cost.
Steel-price movements pressured gross margin under largely fixed-price contracts, while freight remains above original cost assumptions and export enquiries have converted slowly.
The new data-center and high-rise opportunities are early-stage for the company; their size and contribution were not disclosed, and the new orders were post-quarter.

sectorSummary.overview: PEB demand and order pipelines remained healthy, but steel inflation and execution costs constrained profit conversion. Capacity additions and new building applications support the growth outlook; H2 delivery, margin recovery and cash conversion remain important, with EPACK reducing its margin range.

trends.text: Industrial and infrastructure enquiries and order books continue to support execution visibility.
Capacity additions are expanding the addressable market, although several commissioning milestones occurred after Q2.

tailwinds.text: Management expects stronger H2 execution as projects progress and additional capacity ramps.
Data-center and more complex building applications offer new business opportunities; enquiry conversion and revenue timing vary by company.

headwinds.text: Steel-price inflation and the lag in repricing older orders constrain margin recovery.
Larger-project billing and deliberate steel inventories have tied up working capital.

opportunities.text: Interarch is expanding heavy structures and export capabilities to improve margin protection and operating leverage over time.
M&B’s post-quarter data-center/high-rise wins and UK/US West Coast plans create potential new growth avenues.

risks.text: EPACK missed the Q2 margin expectation and its planned quarter-end Ghiloth commissioning, while negative H1 operating cash flow makes collections a priority.
Interarch’s new-vertical expenses precede revenue; M&B’s freight costs remain above original assumptions.

insights.text: Interarch is favoring variable-price orders; M&B still reports largely fixed-price exposure, so steel-risk protection differs.
New capacity and orders disclosed after September-end should be distinguished from Q2 operating delivery.
